545. Boundary of Binary Tree

The boundary of a binary tree is the concatenation of the root, the left boundary, the leaves from left to right, and the right boundary in reverse order.

Left Boundary: Nodes from the root to the leftmost leaf (excluding leaf). If left child exists, go left; else go right.

Right Boundary: Nodes from the root to the rightmost leaf (excluding leaf) in reverse order. If right child exists, go right; else go left.

Leaves: All leaf nodes from left to right.

Example 1:

Input: root = [1,null,2,3,4]
Output: [1,3,4,2]
input_format: Level-order traversal of the binary tree.
output_format: List of integers representing the boundary.
constraints: The number of nodes is in range [1, 10^4]
explanation: Perform three separate traversals: left boundary (excluding leaves), all leaves, and right boundary (excluding leaves, in reverse).
